newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foster's has no comment on buy-back rumours.
newsitem.headline: Foster's has no comment on buy-back rumours.

text.p: Foster's Brewing Group Ltd on Tuesday dismissed as speculation a newspaper report which suggested a major share buy-back was imminent.
The Australian on Tuesday quoted unnamed sources as saying a buy-back could be announced as early as Wednesday, as part of an effort to move two major shareholders from the register.
The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) owns 37 percent of the brewer. Japan's Asahi Brewing owns 14 percent.
Both are said to be keen to sell their holdings.
"That speculation has been going on and on for a couple of months now and we just won't comment on it," Foster's senior vice-president of public affairs, Graeme Willersdorf, said.
"We are making no comment on it at all, and we have consistently done that for the last four months."
BHP also declined to comment. "We can't comment on market speculation," BHP spokesman Michael Spencer told Reuters.
The Australian last week quoted an Asahi spokesman as also declining to comment on the Japanese brewer's stake in Foster's.
The Australian said BHP had written down the book value of its Foster's investment to A$2.33 per share.
In late morning trade on Tuesday, Foster's shares were trading at A$2.66, up one cent from Monday's close.
